claims.statement: Using the accepted private-message 30-row definitions and optimization order of transaction e3c1036ca607539a5ebcddf3058e6014ac5c1cd9, let Q be any N-point posterior grid containing {0,1/2,1}. Every finite-output binary-input receiver has an at-most-N-output replacement with the same mutual-information samples on Q, so inf_{G,K finite} V_Q(G,K) = inf_{|G|,|K|<=N} V_Q(G,K); when Q is reflection closed, inf_{m finite} V_Q(m,m^circ) = inf_{|supp(m)|<=N} V_Q(m,m^circ). For Q0={0,1/2,1} and c=h_2(1/4)-1/2, inf_{G,K finite} V_{Q0}(G,K) = inf_{m finite} V_{Q0}(m,m^circ) = c. Moreover, for every finite-output input-only pair G,K with g=J_G(1/2), k=J_K(1/2), B(G,K) >= V_0(g,k) >= max{F(g),F(k)}, where F(x)=2c max{c,x}/(c+x); consequently, if c <= U < 2c and B(G,K) <= U, then 2c^2/U-c <= g,k <= Uc/(2c-U). These are finite-grid and necessary-coercivity statements only, with no continuum cardinality, limit interchange, or full-functional reflected-optimality assertion.

root/proof/theorem9-cited-premise-founda.summary: Under the exact encoded Theorem 9 premise, the accepted proof sets R0=0, expands all minimum branches and both interval side conditions into 30 scalar rows, and compares them term by term with an independently generated L=3 path system using only the displayed chain-rule normalizations. An exhaustive audit shows that every output-bearing mutual-information term contains only one of Y, G, K, or Z, so replacing G and K by their input-only product marginals preserves every required marginal and every row. The proof then applies the specialized system at fixed q,G,K to obtain the stated receiver-infimum capacity upper-bound formula without interchanging optimization orders. Posterior identities expressed through J_A(t), together with J_A(0)=J_A(1)=0, establish the Q0 midpoint-value reduction; an explicit zero-rate hierarchy and individual-rate rows establish finiteness on the realizable domain. The argument proves only the accepted conditional claim and does not prove or authenticate the assumed Theorem 9 premise or numerically evaluate the receiver infimum.
